# Conformance corpus

The golden-file corpus for Sherd's Markdown dialect. The specification calls
this "the single highest-value test asset" (`QA-002`) — build it first, and grow
it with every bug.

**Target: ≥ 500 cases by the end of phase P0.3.** It is empty right now; the
harness arrives in **P-1.4** and the cases accumulate through P0.1–P0.3.

## Layout

Each case is a directory holding an input and its expected outputs:

```
testdata/conformance/<category>/<case-name>/
├── input.md          # the source document
├── ast.json          # expected AST, including byte ranges (FR-MD-003)
├── metadata.json     # expected extracted metadata: links, tags, properties,
│                     #   headings, blocks, tasks, embeds
└── output.html       # expected rendered HTML
```

A case may omit any expected file it does not exercise. All four comparisons run
for every case that provides them.

## Rules

- **A parser change grows the corpus in the same commit.** Not the next one.
- **Every fixed bug adds a case that fails before the fix** (`QA-012`).
- **Cases are written by hand or generated by Sherd, never copied from another
  project's test suite** — with one exception: the CommonMark specification's
  own test suite, which is licensed for this use and forms the base layer
  (`FR-MD-001`).
- **No real personal notes.** Fixtures are synthetic.
- **No third-party branding** in fixture content (`LEG-003`).

## Priority areas

Code precedence is the most valuable thing in here. Extended syntax must be
inert inside inline code, fenced code, indented code, and math (`FR-MD-028`) —
the specification flags this as the single most common bug class in this
application category, so the corpus should cover every extension against every
code context.
